title: Faithful flatness of completion inside the Jacobson radical
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ be an ideal, where $\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ is the intersection of all maximal ideals. Let $\widehat R_I=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/I^n$ be the adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then the canonical homomorphism $R\to\widehat R_I$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Put $S=\widehat R_I$ and let $c:R\to S$ be the canonical map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] to the Noetherian ring $R$ and its ideal $I$: the map $c$ is flat. This application does not require $R$ to be local.

Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$. Since $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, we have $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], first-coordinate projection is an $R$-algebra map $p:S\to R/I$ with $p(c(a))=a\bmod I$. Compose it with $R/I\to R/\mathfrak m$ to obtain a unital ring map $q:S\to R/\mathfrak m$ satisfying $q(c(a))=a\bmod\mathfrak m$. Every element of the extended ideal $\mathfrak mS$ is a finite sum $\sum_j c(a_j)s_j$ with $a_j\in\mathfrak m$, so $q(\sum_jc(a_j)s_j)=0$. If $1$ belonged to $\mathfrak mS$, this would give $1=0$ in $R/\mathfrak m$, contradicting the properness of $\mathfrak m$. Hence $\mathfrak mS\ne S$.

The map $c:R\to S$ is flat by Step 1, and Step 2 shows that $\mathfrak mS\ne S$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] to conclude that $c$ is faithfully flat.
